transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, I'm a high school teacher, and I came in because... I'm just having a really hard time staying focused on my work. 

I can sit down with a stack of essays to grade, or a new curriculum document, fully intending to just get it done. But then, within ten minutes, I'll realize I’ve just been staring at the exact same page. My mind will be off thinking about three other things, and I'm barely taking in a single word of what’s right in front of me. It's just getting really frustrating to deal with.
Has this difficulty with staying focused been something you've struggled with for most of your life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

It's definitely not new. It's... yeah, it's been most of my life, really. Even back in primary school, my report cards always said things like I was "bright but careless," or that I wouldn't finish my work unless I was closely supervised. And my parents were constantly finding crumpled up worksheets shoved at the bottom of my backpack that I had just completely forgotten to turn in. So, yeah, it's always been a struggle.
Beyond the difficulty with focus, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or uninterested in things you usually enjoy for most of the past two years?

No, I haven't really felt like that. I mean, I definitely get frustrated with myself when I fall behind on grading or feel like I'm messing up at work, but I wouldn't say I feel sad or down overall. I still enjoy my usual hobbies and everything. It's really just the focus and getting things done that's the problem.
Do you often find yourself feeling restless, like you have an internal motor that won't turn off, or do you frequently interrupt others when they are speaking?

No, not really. I don't feel restless like that, and I don't think I have a habit of interrupting people. I can sit perfectly still at my desk for hours... the problem is just that my brain is completely somewhere else while I'm doing it. So, no, I don't feel like I have an internal motor or anything. It's really just the mental focus that's the issue.
Outside of your work, do you often find yourself losing things, forgetting appointments, or struggling to keep your personal living space organized?

Yeah, definitely. Losing things is a huge issue for me. I'm constantly hunting for things I need for the day... like my classroom keys, my lesson notes, or my USB drive. I also do some refereeing, and I'm always misplacing my whistle and cards for that. 

It drives me crazy because I'll be tearing the place apart looking for something, even when I'm absolutely sure I just had it in my hand like five minutes earlier. I just set things down and they vanish. So, yeah, keeping track of my stuff and keeping things organized is definitely a constant struggle.

Do you often avoid or find yourself reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort, like preparing reports or completing long forms, because you find the process so mentally draining?

No, I wouldn't say I avoid them. I mean, I know I have to do things like write up detailed lesson plans or grade long essays, and I do sit down to do them. I don't really put them off because they feel mentally draining or anything like that. 

Like I was saying before, the issue is more about keeping my brain on track once I'm actually doing the work. I don't dread starting the tasks, I just struggle to stay focused on them once I'm at my desk. So, no, I don't really avoid them.
Have you ever been told by others, such as friends, family, or colleagues, that you act without thinking or that you seem impulsive in your actions?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really had anyone tell me that. I'm pretty thoughtful about what I do, and I don't really make snap decisions or do things out of the blue. So, no, impulsivity isn't really something that's come up with my friends or at work.
